questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following characteristics is are exhibited by $\mathrm{C}_4$-plants?
I. Kranz anatomy.
II. The first product of photosynthesis is oxaloacetic acid.
III. Both PEP carboxylates and ribulose biphosphate carboxylate act as carboxylating enzymes.
The correct option is
options: I and III, but not II
I and II, but not III
II and III, but not I
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{C}_4$-plants have an alternative $\mathrm{CO}_2$ fixation pathway called Hatch and Slack cycle. These plants have Kranz anatomy in leaf, where vascular bundles are surrounded by bundle sheath.
In $\mathrm{C}_4$ cycle light reaction occurs in, mesophyll chloroplast by PEP carboxylaes and the assimilation of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ takes place in, i.e., dark phase in bundle sheath chloroplast by Rubisco.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In photosynthesis carbon dioxide is converted to carbohydrates. It is a _______ process.
questions.solution: Photosynthesis is an oxidation reduction process in which water is oxidised and carbon dioxide is reduced to carbohydrates. Hence, it is anabolic and endergonic process.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Hormone inducing fruit ripening is
questions.solution: Ethylene is a natural gaseous hormone, which is predominantly known for inducing fruit ripening.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following properties is shown by cytokinins?
questions.solution: Cytokinin is a plant growth hormone, which is mostly synthesised in the roots, cytokinin delays leaf senescence.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Genetic dwarfism can be overcome by
questions.solution: Genetic dwarfism is overcome by the usage of gibberellins. Ethylene is a gaseous hormone, which induces ripening in unripe fruits. ABA cause ageing and abscission of leaves.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: Zeatin is a cytokinin. IAA or indole acetic acid is a natural auxin. IBA or indole butyric acid and NAA or nepthalene acetic acid are synthetic auxin.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Cycas revoluta is popularly known as
questions.solution: A starch called sago is obtained from the pith of Cycas revoluta. That is why it is called sago palm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of plants are not seed producers?
questions.solution: Seed producing plants belong to spermatophyta. It includes gymnosperms and angiosperms. Seed orginated in gymnosperms. Fern and Funaria belong to pteridophytes and bryophytes respectively. So, they do not reproduce by producing seeds.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: Pteridophyte are called vascular cryptogams. They are seedless vascular plant as they possess water conducting xylem and food translocating phloem but do not produce seed (instead spare formation takes place).

questions.solution:

Agar is a jelly, like substance used for culturing processes. It is used as laxatives in bacteriological and mycological media.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is heterosporous?
questions.solution: The sporophyte of pteridophyte produces meiospores inside sporangia, which may be homosporous (e.g., Adiantum, Dryopteris, Equisetum, etc.) or heterosporous (e.g., Salvinia, Selaginella, etc.)

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: Parthenogenesis is a form of sexual reproduction in which the ovum develops into a new individual without fertilisation.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: Endosperm of gymnosperm is a pre-fertilisation tissue. It is basically the female gametophyte hence it is haploid unlike triploid in angiosperm.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of increasing acidic strength is
options: phenol \lt  ethanol \lt  chloroacetic acid \lt  acetic acid
ethanol \lt  phenol \lt  chloroacetic acid \lt  acetic acid
ethanol \lt  phenol \lt  acetic acid \lt  chloroacetic acid
chloroacetic acid \lt  acetic acid \lt  phenol \lt  ethanol
questions.solution:
Due to - I effect of Cl , chloroacetic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid. Further dur to stablisation of phenoxide ion by resonance and no such stabilisation in case of ethoxide ion, phenol is a stronger acid than ethanol.
Hence, overall acid strength increases in the order; ethanol \lt  phenol \lt  acetic acid \lt  chloroacetic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The value of $K_c$ for the reaction,
$2 A \rightleftharpoons B+C$ is $2 \times 10^{-3}$. At a given time, if the composition of reaction mixture is $[A]=[B]=[C]=3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{M}$. Which is true?
options: The reaction will proceed in forward direction
The reaction will proceed in backward direction
The reaction will proceed in any direction
questions.solution:
Reaction quotient, $Q_C=[B][C] /[A]^2$ as
as
$[A]=[B]=[C]=3 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{M}Q_C=\left(3 \times 10^{-4}\right) \times\left(3 \times 10^{-4}\right) /\left(3 \times 10^{-4}\right)^2=1$
As $Q_C \gt K_c$, so the reaction will proceed in the reverse direction.

questions.q: Which of the following statement is correct?
options: $E_{\text {cell }}$ and $\Delta_t G$ of cell reaction both are extensive properties.
$E_{\text {cell }}$ and $\Delta_r G$ of cell reaction both are intensive properties.
$E_{\text {cell }}$ in the intensive property while $\Delta_r G$ of cell reaction is an extensive property.
$E_{\text {cell }}$ is an extensive property while $\Delta_r G$ of cell reaction is an intensive property.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{O}_2(g) \longrightarrow \mathrm{O}_3(g) ; K_p$ for this reaction is $2.47 \times 10^{-29}$. At $298 \mathrm{~K}, \Delta_r G^{\circ}$ for conversion of oxygen to ozone will be
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \Delta_r G^{\circ}= & 2.303 \operatorname{log~Kp}\left(R=8.314 \mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right) \\ \Delta_r G^{\circ}= & -2.303 \times 8.314 \mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \times 298 \mathrm{~K} \\ & \times \log 2.47 \times 10^{-29} \\ = & 163000 \mathrm{Jmol}^{-1}=163 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: $220 \mathrm{~V}, 50 \mathrm{~Hz}, \mathrm{AC}$ source is connected to an inductance of 0.2 H and a resistance of $20 \Omega$ in series. What is the current in the circuit?
questions.solution:
From the formula
$\begin{aligned} I & =\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^2+(\omega L)^2}} \\ I & =\frac{220}{\sqrt{(20)^2+(2 \pi \times 50 \times 0.2)^2}} \\ & =\frac{220}{66}=3.33 \mathrm{~A}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Ionisation potential of hydrogen atom is 13.6 eV . Hydrogen atom on the ground state rarely excited by monochromatic radiation of photon 12.1 eV . The special line emitted by a hydrogen atom according to Bohr's theory will be
questions.solution:
From the relation
$E_3-E_1=(-1.5)-(-13.6)=12.1$
As the energy is equal to the energy taken by $n=1, n=2, n=3$. Hence there will be three spectral line.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A parallel plate condenser is filled with two dielectrics as shown in figure. Area of each pate is $A \mathrm{~m}^2$ and the separation is $d$ metre. The dielectric constants are $K_1$ and $K_2$ respectively. Its capacitance in farad will be
questions.solution:
From the formula
$\begin{aligned} C & =\frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{\frac{1}{k_1}+\frac{1}{k_2}}=\frac{\varepsilon_0 A}{t}\left(\frac{k_1 k_2}{k_1+k_2}\right) \\ & =\frac{2 \varepsilon_0 A}{d}\left(\frac{k_1 k_2}{k_1+k_2}\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The equivalent resistance across $A$ and $B$ is
questions.solution: The equivalent circuit can be redrawn as We have, $\frac{P}{Q}=\frac{R}{S}$ i.e, $\quad \frac{4}{4}=\frac{4}{4}$ So, the given circuit is a balanced Wheatstone's bridge. Hence, the equivalent resistance $\begin{aligned} R_{A B} & =\frac{(4+4) \times(4+4)}{(4+4)+(4+4)}=\frac{8 \times 8}{8+8} \\ & =\frac{64}{16}=4 \Omega\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: At room temperature, copper has free electron density of $8.4 \times 10^{28} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}$. The electron drift velocity in a copper conductor of cross-sectional area of $10^{-6} \mathrm{~m}^2$ and carrying a current of 5.4 A , will be
questions.solution:
Drift velocity in a copper conductor
$\begin{aligned} v_d=\frac{i}{n e A} & =\frac{5.4}{8.4 \times 10^{28} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 10^{-6}} \\ & =0.4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~ms}^{-1} \\ & =0.4 \mathrm{mms}^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 5 amp fuse wire can withstand a maximum power of 1 W in circuit. The resistance of the fuse wire is
questions.solution:
Power $P=i^2 R\Rightarrow \quad R=\frac{P}{i^2}$
given, $P=1 \mathrm{~W}$, and $i=5 \mathrm{~A}\therefore \quad R=\frac{1}{(5)^2}=0.04 \Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform wire of resistance $R$ and length $L$ is cut into four equal parts, each of length $L / 4$ which are then connected in parallel combination. The effective resistance of the combination will be
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{ll}R=\frac{\rho l}{A} \text { or } R \propto l \\ \therefore & \frac{R_1}{R_2}=\frac{I_1}{I_2}=\frac{L}{L / 4}=4 \\ \text { or } & R_2=\frac{R}{4}\left(\because R_1=R\right)\end{array}
In parallel combination of such four resistance
$\frac{1}{R^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{R_2}+\frac{1}{R_1}+\frac{1}{R_2}+\frac{1}{R_2}$
or $\quad \frac{1}{R^{\prime}}=\frac{1}{R / 4}+\frac{1}{R / 4}+\frac{1}{R / 4}+\frac{1}{R / 4}$
or $\quad \frac{1}{R^{\prime}}=\frac{4}{R}+\frac{4}{R}+\frac{4}{R}+\frac{4}{R}$
or $\quad \frac{1}{R^{\prime}}=\frac{16}{R}$
or $\quad R^{\prime}=R / 16

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Minimum excitation potential of Bohr's first orbit in hydrogen atom is
questions.solution:
From the relation
$\begin{aligned} \Delta E & =13.6 \mathrm{eV}-\frac{13.6 \mathrm{eV}}{n^2} \\ & =13.6 \mathrm{eV}-\frac{13.6 \mathrm{eV}}{(2)^2}=10.2 \mathrm{eV}\end{aligned}$
Therefore, excitation potential
$=\frac{10.2}{e} \mathrm{eV}=10.2 \mathrm{~V}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The work function for metals $A, B$ and $C$ are respectively $1.92 \mathrm{eV}, 2.0 \mathrm{eV}$ and 5 eV. According to Einstein's equation the metals which will emit photo, electrons for a radiation of wavelength $4100 Å$ is/are
questions.solution:
Work function for wavelength of $4100 Å$ is
$\begin{aligned} W & =\frac{h c}{\lambda} \\ & =\frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{4100 \times 10^{-10}} \\ & =4.8 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{~J} \\ & =\frac{4.8 \times 10^{-19}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}} \mathrm{eV} \\ & =3 \mathrm{eV}\end{aligned}$
Now, we have
$\begin{aligned} & W_A=1.22 \mathrm{eV} \\ & W_B=2.0 \mathrm{eV} \\ & W_C=5 \mathrm{eV}\end{aligned}$
Since, $W_A \lt W$
and $W_B \lt W$, hence $A$ and $B$ will emit photoelectrons.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In 0.2 s, the current in a coil increases from 2.0 A to 3.0 A. If inductance of coil is 60 mH, then induced current in external resistance of $3 \Omega$ will be
questions.solution:
Induced emf
$\begin{aligned}|e| & =L \frac{d i}{d t}=\left(60 \times 10^{-3}\right) \times \frac{(3.0-2.0)}{0.2} \\ & =\frac{60 \times 10^{-3} \times 1}{0.2}=0.3 \mathrm{~V}\end{aligned}$
Induced current,
$\mathrm{t} i=\frac{e}{R}=\frac{0.3}{3}=0.1 \mathrm{~A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The escape velocity for the earth is $11.2 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{s}$. The mass of another planet 100 times mass of earth and its radius is 4 times radius of the earth. The escape velocity for the planet is
questions.solution:
The escape velocity of the the planet
$\begin{aligned} v_{\text {escape }} & =\sqrt{\frac{2 G m}{R}} \propto \sqrt{\frac{M}{R}} \\ \frac{v_p}{v_e} & =\sqrt{\frac{M_p}{R_p} \times \frac{R_e}{M_e}} \\ \frac{v_p}{v_e} & =\sqrt{100 \times \frac{1}{4}}=5 \\ v_p & =5 \times 11.2=56 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{s}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The speed of air flow on the upper and lower surfaces of a wing of an aeroplane are $v_1$ and $v_2$ respectively. If $A$ is the cross section area of the wing and $\rho$ is the density of air, then the upward life is
questions.solution:
\(\begin{aligned}
E_{\text {rotational }} & \left.=\frac{1}{2} \right\rvert\, \omega^2 \\
& =\frac{\mathrm{L}^2}{2 \mid} \quad(\because \mathrm{L}=\mid \omega)
\end{aligned}\)
Therefore, \(\mathrm{L}^2=2 \mathrm{EI}\)
Hence \(L_A^2=2 E_A I_A\) ...(i)
and \(L_B^2=2 E_B I_B\) ...(ii)
From equation (i) and (ii)
\(\begin{aligned}
\frac{L_A}{L_B} & =\sqrt{\frac{2 E_A I_A}{2 E_B I_B}} \\
& =\sqrt{\frac{100}{4}} \\
\frac{L_A}{L_B} & =5 \\
\left(\because \frac{E_B}{E_A}\right. & \left.=100 \text { and } \frac{I_A}{I_B}=4\right)
\end{aligned}\)

questions.q: The work done in increasing the size of a soap film for $10 \mathrm{~cm} \times 6 \mathrm{~m}$ to $10 \mathrm{~cm} \times 11 \mathrm{~cm}$ is $3 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~J}$. The surface tension of the film is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two boys are standing at the ends $A$ and $B$ of a ground, where $A B=a$. The boy at $B$ starts running in a direction perpendicular to $A B$ with velocity $v_1$. The boy at $A$ starts running simultaneously with velocity $v$ and catches the other boy in a time $t$, where $t$ is
questions.solution: Distance covered by boy $A$ in time $tA C=v t\ldots(i)$ Distance covered by boy $B$ in time $tB C=v_1 t\ldots(ii)$ Using Pythagoras theorem $\begin{aligned} A C^2 & =A B^2+B C^2 \\ \text { or } \quad(v t)^2 & =a^2+\left(v_1 t\right)^2\end{aligned}$ or $\quad v^2 t^2-v_1^2 t^2=a^2$ or $\quad t^2\left(v^2-v_1^2\right)=a^2 \therefore t=\sqrt{\frac{a^2}{\left(v^2-v_1^2\right)}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two equal negative charges $-q$ are fixed at the point $(0, a)$ and $(0,-a)$ on the $y$-axis. A positive charge $Q$ is released from rest at the point $(2 a, 0)$ on the $x$-axis. The charge will
options: move to the origin and remain at rest
questions.solution: Component of force on charge of $+Q$ at $P$, along $x$-axis, $\begin{aligned} F_x & =\frac{2 Q q}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0\left(a^2+x^2\right)} \times \frac{x}{\sqrt{a^2+x^2}} \\ & =\frac{2 Q q x}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0\left(a^2+x^2\right)} \times \frac{x}{\sqrt{a^2+x^2}} \\ & =\frac{2 Q q x}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0\left(a^2+x^2\right)^{3 / 2}}\end{aligned}$ Which is not directly proportional to $x$. So, motion is oscillatory but not SHM.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two simple pendulums of length 0.5 m and 20 m respectively are given small linear displacement in one direction at the same time. They will again be in the phase when the pendulum of shorter length has completed $x$ oscillations, where $x$ is
questions.solution:
Time period of simple pendulum
For Ist pendulum $\begin{aligned} T_1 & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{5}{g}} \\ & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{5}{9.8}}=\sqrt{20} \mathrm{~s}\end{aligned}$
For IInd pendulum $T_2=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{20}{g}}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{20}{9.8}}=2 \sqrt{20} \mathrm{~s}$
Suppose the time will be in same phase is $t$ then
$\begin{aligned} \frac{1}{t} & =\frac{1}{T_1}-\frac{1}{T_2} \\ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{20}}-\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{20}}\end{aligned}=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{20}}$
So, $\quad t=2 \sqrt{20}$
Hence, the number of oscillation of simple pendulum of shorter length $(x)=\frac{2 \sqrt{20}}{\sqrt{20}}=2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A luminous object is placed at a distance of 30 cm from the convex lens of focal length 20 cm . On the other side of the lens, at what distance from the lens a convex mirror of radius of curvature 10 cm be placed in order to have an upright image of the object coincident with it
questions.solution: Using the formula $\begin{aligned} \frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{u} & =\frac{1}{f} \\ \frac{1}{v}-\frac{1}{-30} & =\frac{1}{20} \\ v & =60 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$ If the image is formed at the centre of curvature of the mirror, the coincidence is possible. Then the rays refracting through the lens will fall normally on the convex mirror and retrace their path of form the image at $O$. Hence, the distance between lens and mirror will be $60-10=50 \mathrm{~cm}$.

So, $\quad \tan i=\frac{3}{4}=\frac{r}{4}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Two rigid bodies $A$ and $B$ rotate with rotational kinetic energies $E_A$ and $E_B$ respectively. The moments of inertia of $A$ and $B$ about the axis of rotation are $I_A$ and $I_B$ respectively.
If $I_A=\frac{I_B}{4}$ and $E_A=100=E_B$, the ratio of angular momentum $\left(L_A\right)$ of $A$ to the angular momentum $\left(L_B\right)$ of $B$ is
questions.solution:
From, the formula, rotational KE
$E_{\text {rotational }}=\frac{1}{2} l \omega^2=\frac{L^2}{2 \mid}(\because L=\mid \omega)$
Therefore, $\quad L^2=2 E l$
Hence
$L_A^2=2 E_A I_A\ldots(i)$
and
$L_B^2=2 E_B I_B\ldots(ii)$
From Eq. (i) and (ii)
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{L_A}{L_B}=\sqrt{\frac{2 E_A I_B}{2 E_B I_A}}=\sqrt{\frac{100}{4}}=5 \\ & \quad\left(\because \frac{E_B}{E_A}=100 \text { and } \frac{I_A}{I_B}=4\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which logic gate is represented by the following combination of logic gates?
questions.solution: Output of gate $1, Y_1=\bar{A}$ Output of gate $2, Y_2=\bar{B}$ Output of gate 3 , $\begin{aligned} Y & =\overline{Y_1+Y_2}=\overline{\bar{A}+\bar{B}} \\ & =\overline{\bar{A}} \times \overline{\bar{B}} \\ & =A B\end{aligned}$ Which is the output of AND gate.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two coherent light beams of intensities $I$ and $4 I$ are superposed. The maximum and minimum possible intensities in the resulting beam are
questions.solution:
The net intensity due to interference of two beams of intensities \(\mathrm{I}_1, \mathrm{I}_2\) with a phase difference of \(\phi\) is
\(\mathrm{I}_{\text {net }}=\mathrm{I}_1+\mathrm{I}_2+2 \sqrt{\mathrm{I}_1} \sqrt{\mathrm{I}_2} \cos \phi\)
Thus, \(\mathrm{I}_{\text {net }_{\text {max }}}\) occurs for \(\cos \phi=1\)
\(\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}_{\text {net }_{\max }}=\left(\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_1}+\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_2}\right)^2=9 \mathrm{I}\)
Similarly, \(\mathrm{I}_{\text {net }_{\min }}\) occurs for \(\cos \phi=-1\)
\(\Rightarrow \mathrm{I}_{\text {net }_{\min }}=\left(\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_1}-\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_2}\right)^2=\mathrm{I}\)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following statements best characterise the testis?
options: The seminiferous epithelium contains only proliferative cells
Functional compartmentalisation of the seminiferous epithelium depends on tight junctions
The interstitial tissue contains few capillaries
The seminiferous epithelium contains numerous capillaries
questions.solution: Each testis contains seminiferous tubules for spermatogenesis and interstitial (Intertubullar) tissue rich in Leyding cells for steroidgenesis. Seminiferous epithelium contains a continuous layer of Sertoli cells, which are joined by tight intercellular junctions. These junctions divide the epithelium into a basal compartment that contains spermatogonia and an abdominal compartment.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Drugs that cause malformation in developing embryo during pregancy are called
questions.solution: Teratogens is an agent that can cause malformations of an embryo on foetus. This can be a chemical substance, a virus or ionising radiation. Mostly, during first three months of pregnancy the pregnant lady should avoid all contact with teratogen.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Hormone responsible for the secretion of milk after parturition is
questions.solution: Prolactin or luteotrophic hormone or luteotrophin is a hormone, synthesised and stored in the anterior pituitary gland, that stimulates milk production after child birth and also stimulates production of progesterone by the corpus luteum in the ovary.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Biological treatment of water pollution is done with the help of
questions.solution: Water hyacinth (phytoplankton), can purify water polluted by biological and chemical wastes-water hyacinth has remarkable capacity to accumulate poisonous metals including radioactive substances.

questions.solution: A mature ovarian follicle is called Graafian follicle. After ovulation, the empty Graafian follicle shows deposition of luetin and forms corpus luteum that ultimately degenerates.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In DNA, when AGCT occurs, their association is as per which of the following pair
questions.solution: DNA molecule has four bases-adenine guanine cytosine and thymine. Adenine always pairs with thymine and guanine pairs with cytosine. Their association is A-T and G-C.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A segment of DNA has 120 adenine and 120 cytosine bases. The total number of nucleotides present in the segment is
questions.solution:
According to Chargaff's rules, the amount of adenine is always equal to that of thymine, and the amount of guanine is always equal to that of cytosine.
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{A} & =\mathrm{T}(120) \\ \mathrm{G} & =\mathrm{C}(120)\end{aligned}$
The total number of nucleotides would be $120 \times 4=480$.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The largest gene in man is
questions.solution: The largest known gene in human is the dystrophin gene, which has 79 axons spanning at least 2300 kb . The human dystrophin gene requires 16 hours to be transcribed.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Predation and parasitism are which type of interactions.
questions.solution: Both predation and parasitism show negative interactions. In negative interaction one species is harmed ( - ) while the other is benefitted.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following plant keeps its stomata open during night and closed during the day?
questions.solution: Scotoactive mechanism of opening of stomata is seen in fleshy xerophytes like Opuntia, cactus, etc. They keep their stomata open at night and closed during daytimes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following cells in earthworm play a role similar to liver in vertebrates?
questions.solution: Chlorogogen cells are excretory in function. The chlorogogen cells take up excretory matter from the blood capillaries of the gut and from the coelomic fluid of the coelom. They also store glycogen and fat. So, these cells are analogous to the liver of vertebrates.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Yellow bone marrow is found specially in the medullary cavity
questions.solution: Bone marrow is of two types; red and yellow. The yellow marrow is found especially in medullary cavity of long bones, while red is in spongy bones.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What will happen if ligaments are torn?
options: Bone less movable at joint and pain
Bone will move freely at joint and no pain
questions.solution: Ligaments join a bone with another bone in movable/synovial joints. Torn ligaments make movement at joints very painful and restricted. It heals only after prolonged movement restriction.
